reader.requirement: At --std 85 the value DAY-OF-INTEGER returns is an integer of the form YYYYDDD: the Gregorian year times 1000 plus the day of that year (001-365/366), so a 9(4)/9(3) split of a 9(7) receiver gives the year and the day.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 window sig.IntroducedIn (85): admitted at 85
DialectBehavior.IntegerDateFormBounded inactive at 85: the YYYY part may exceed 9999 (YYYYDDD with a five-digit year)

reader.edition-search: as for RV1; the year*1000+day composition in CobolDate.DayOfInteger takes no edition input.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only past 9999-12-31, where 85 returns e.g. 10000001 (year 10000, day 001) and 2023 returns 0; the form year*1000+day is the same code.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f35_03 checks the form through a 9(4)/9(3) REDEFINES at 2000366; the leap-day day 366 and the day-001 forms are covered, a year of more than four digits is not.

probes.printed: SPLIT YYYY=2000 DDD=366 (the witness's recorded output)

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.13.4 RV2  (2.13.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV2

reader.notes: The returned value is year*1000 + day of year from one Gregorian day count; the 1985 arm only lifts the 9999 cap, which the 1989 text never set. A year beyond 9999 yields more than seven digits, which RV2's YYYY reads as four digits; with no upper bound in the 1989 argument rule, the five-digit year is the only value the rule can mean, so this is recorded as conforming.

refuter.evidence: Same probe rdoi1-001: every value is year*1000 + day of year, including day 366 of 3600 and year 1900's day 365. The only contestable point is a year above 9999 (five or more digits of YYYY): under the reading that RV2's four-letter YYYY implicitly bounds the argument, such an argument violates a constraint and the result is undefined (§1989 A.1.2.2), so any value conforms; under the reader's reading the value year*1000+day is the only one RV2 can mean. Either reading leaves the compiler conforming. cite.py: OK  §1989:A.2.13.4 RV2  (2.13.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV2.
